tldr: Public compatibility preferences change the uncertainty of randomized group interventions even when all potential group outcomes are fixed. For every fixed public \(\Lambda\in[1,1+\sqrt2)\), complete nonpartite triple formation with arbitrary positive weights of ratio at most \(\Lambda\) admits a primitive uniform \(G^{-1/8}\) Gaussian approximation for the original group contrast under a positive full formation-plus-assignment variance floor. The proved spine supplies the nonpartite tilt bound, the entropy-to-variance comparison, the leading causal variance projection, and asymptotic conservativeness of ordinary observed arm variances. A separate total observable connected interval has finite 90-percent coverage and length bounded by a constant depending only on \(\Lambda,v\) times the actual design standard deviation. The theorem includes exactly zero conditional assignment noise. Common scaling of weights changes none of these conclusions; the angular endpoint is excluded, and the sharper Gaussian rate remains open. This is a subfield technical benchmark for moderate soft compatibility.
